item: a mailbox pull over TLS checks the server's certificate chain and name, and refuses honestly when either fails
key_paths: src/ingest/email.py; tests/test_mailbox_tls_verify_r650.py; tests/_mailbox_tls_pki.py; tests/test_mailbox_stall_r647.py; tests/test_mailbox_stop_r640.py; docs/SECURITY.md; docs/USER_MANUAL.md
summary: imaplib.IMAP4_SSL and poplib.POP3_SSL fall back to ssl._create_stdlib_context(), which verifies neither the chain nor the host name, so LOGIN/PASS went to whoever answered for the server. Every mailbox pull now hands them ssl.create_default_context() (the platform trust store, CERT_REQUIRED, check_hostname), a fresh one per pull; a failed check raises MailboxCertificateError naming the host and OpenSSL's cause before any command is sent, with no fallback and no switch that turns the check off. Tests run real imaplib/poplib against loopback TLS servers with a throwaway authority: self-signed and wrong-name certificates are refused with no command received, a trusted one pulls as before. Release line: a newsletter mailbox pull over TLS now checks the mail server's certificate and refuses, saying why, if it does not match the server's name or is not from an authority your computer trusts, before your password is sent.
